images.name: hero-wrapped
images.prompt:
A residential living room part-way through a contents pack-out. An armchair and a sofa are covered in clear protective plastic sheeting taped at the base. Beside them, a stack of plain brown moving boxes sits closed and labelled with handwriting on the side. A houseplant and a side table are still in place behind. The room is otherwise undisturbed — this is protection in progress, not damage.

COMPOSITION — this sits beside page copy on the right half of a hero. Keep the plastic-wrapped furniture and the box stack together in frame with a little room above. No people in shot.

Shot on a job by a restoration technician on a mid-range phone — a working record, not a photograph anyone meant to be seen.
LIGHT: whatever was already in the room. Ordinary ceiling fixtures or grey daylight through a window. Mixed colour temperature is fine. No sun shafts, no golden hour, no backlighting, no blown-out areas.
SURFACES: everything has history. Scuffed skirting, roller texture on paint, worn carpet, a chipped door frame. Nothing looks recently renovated or staged.
CAMERA: handheld at chest height, slightly off-level. Natural phone depth of field, most of the frame in focus. Mild sensor noise. Flat, slightly muted colour as a phone JPEG renders it, not graded.
DO NOT PRODUCE: glossy or mirror-finish surfaces; evenly lit rooms with no shadow falloff; staged or symmetrical composition; saturated or teal-and-orange colour; shallow depth of field with heavy background blur; lens flare; bokeh; readable text or brand logos on boxes or equipment; HDR-looking shadow lift.
If it looks like a product shot or a stock photo, it is wrong.

4:3 landscape, roughly 1600x1200.
